# SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Supply Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of April 1, 2023 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Meideis Glassworks, Inc.**, a Pennsylvania corporation with its principal place of business at 2200 Furnace Road, Allentown, Pennsylvania 18109 ("**Supplier**"), and **Besouth Facade Systems, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal place of business at 410 Wharf Street, Camden, New Jersey 08103 ("**Buyer**"). Supplier and Buyer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier manufactures and fabricates coated architectural glass, including low-E coated insulating glass units, for commercial building envelopes.

B. Buyer designs, fabricates and installs curtain-wall, window-wall and facade systems for commercial and institutional construction projects.

C. Buyer wishes to purchase, and Supplier wishes to supply, insulating glass units for incorporation into Buyer's facade systems on the terms of this Agreement.

The Parties therefore agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly Controls, is Controlled by, or is under common Control with that Party.

1.2 "**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which commercial banks in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania are authorized or required to close.

1.3 "**Change of Control**" means (a) any direct or indirect transfer, sale or other disposition, whether in a single transaction or a series of related transactions and whether by merger, stock or equity sale, operation of law or otherwise, of more than 50% of the equity interests of Buyer or of any entity that Controls Buyer; or (b) any transaction or series of related transactions as a result of which any person or group of persons acquires the power, directly or indirectly, to direct the management and policies of Buyer.

1.4 "**Committed Quantity**" means the quantity of Products that Buyer commits to purchase for a Project, as stated in the applicable Statement of Work.

1.5 "**Control**" means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct the management and policies of an entity, whether through ownership of voting securities or membership interests, by contract or otherwise; "**Controls**" and "**Controlled**" have correlative meanings.

1.6 "**Price**" means the unit price for a Product determined in accordance with Section 6 and Exhibit B.

1.7 "**Products**" means low-E coated insulating glass units described in Exhibit A.

1.8 "**Project**" means a construction project for which Buyer supplies facade systems incorporating Products.

1.9 "**Purchase Order**" means a written order for Products issued by Buyer under this Agreement and, where applicable, a Statement of Work.

1.10 "**Specifications**" means the technical, performance and dimensional requirements for the Products set out in Exhibit A, together with any Project-specific requirements stated in a Statement of Work or Purchase Order and accepted by Supplier.

1.11 "**Statement of Work**" means a written statement of work for a Project, executed by both Parties and referencing this Agreement, that sets out the Project, the Committed Quantity, the delivery schedule and any Project-specific Specifications.

## 2. SCOPE; STATEMENTS OF WORK

2.1 **Supply.** During the Term, Supplier shall manufacture and sell Products to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase Products from Supplier, in accordance with this Agreement, each applicable Statement of Work and each accepted Purchase Order.

2.2 **Statements of Work.** The Parties may from time to time enter into Statements of Work for particular Projects. Each Statement of Work is incorporated into and governed by this Agreement. A Statement of Work remains "open" from its execution until Supplier has delivered, and Buyer has paid for, the full Committed Quantity under it.

2.3 **Committed Quantities.** Buyer shall purchase the full Committed Quantity stated in each Statement of Work. Buyer may increase a Committed Quantity by Purchase Order, subject to Supplier's acceptance, but may reduce a Committed Quantity only with Supplier's written consent.

## 3. TERM

3.1 **Initial Term.** This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for four years from the Supply Agreement Effective Date (the "**Initial Term**"). For purposes of this Section 3, the "Supply Agreement Effective Date" is the Effective Date.

3.2 **Renewal.** Upon expiration of the Initial Term, and upon expiration of each Renewal Term, this Agreement shall renew automatically for successive periods of three years (each, a "**Renewal Term**" and, together with the Initial Term, the "**Term**"), unless either Party delivers written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least 180 days prior to the expiration of the then-current term. A notice of non-renewal is effective only if delivered in accordance with Section 17.2 at least 180 days before expiration of the then-current term. Each Renewal Term shall be on the terms of this Agreement then in effect, including Section 5.

3.3 **Open Statements of Work.** Expiration of this Agreement does not affect any Statement of Work then open, which shall continue to be governed by this Agreement until completed.

## 4. ORDERING

4.1 **Purchase Orders.** Buyer shall order Products by issuing Purchase Orders that identify the Project, Product type, glass makeup, quantity, dimensions, requested delivery dates and delivery location.

4.2 **Acceptance.** Supplier shall accept or reject each Purchase Order in writing within five Business Days after receipt. Supplier shall not reject a Purchase Order that conforms to this Agreement and to an open Statement of Work. A Purchase Order not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

4.3 **Forecasts.** On or before the fifth Business Day of each calendar quarter, Buyer shall provide Supplier with a non-binding rolling twe

lve-month forecast of its anticipated requirements for Products.

4.4 **Conflicting Terms.** Any pre-printed or additional terms in a Purchase Order, acknowledgment or invoice are of no effect.

## 5. EXCLUSIVITY

5.1 **Requirements.** During the Term, Buyer shall purchase from Supplier 100% of Buyer's requirements for Products for all Projects, and shall not purchase Products from any other source, except as provided in Section 5.2.

5.2 **Supply Failure.** If Supplier notifies Buyer that it cannot supply a Product in the quantity or by the delivery date required by an accepted Purchase Order, or fails to deliver conforming Products within fifteen Business Days after the confirmed delivery date, Buyer may purchase the affected quantity from a third party for that Purchase Order only, and those purchases shall count toward any Committed Quantity.

5.3 **Owner-Directed Sources.** Section 5.1 does not apply to any Product that a Project owner or architect requires, by written specification issued before Buyer's bid, to be purchased from a named source other than Supplier.

## 6. PRICING

6.1 **Prices.** Prices for Products are set out in Exhibit B. Prices are stated per square foot of finished unit area, FCA Supplier's facility in Allentown, Pennsylvania, and exclude applicable sales and use taxes.

6.2 **Annual Adjustment.** Supplier may adjust the Prices once per contract year, effective on each anniversary of the Effective Date, by written notice delivered at least sixty days in advance. No annual adjustment may exceed the greater of 4% or the percentage change in the Producer Price Index for Flat Glass (BLS series PCU327211327211) for the preceding twelve months.

6.3 **Project Pricing.** Prices stated in an executed Statement of Work are fixed for the Committed Quantity under that Statement of Work and are not subject to adjustment under Section 6.2.

## 7. INVOICING AND PAYMENT

7.1 **Invoices.** Supplier shall invoice Buyer upon shipment of each delivery.

7.2 **Payment.** Buyer shall pay each undisputed invoice within forty-five days after receipt. Amounts not paid when due bear interest at 1% per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law if lower.

7.3 **Disputes.** Buyer shall notify Supplier in writing of any good-faith invoice dispute within twenty days after receipt, stating the basis of the dispute, and shall pay the undisputed portion when due. The Parties shall work in good faith to resolve the dispute within thirty days.

## 8. DELIVERY; TITLE AND RISK OF LOSS

8.1 **Delivery.** Supplier shall deliver Products FCA Supplier's facility (Incoterms 2020), packed on Supplier-owned A-frame or L-frame racks, to the carrier designated by Buyer, or, where a Purchase Order so requests, shall arrange freight to the delivery location at Buyer's cost.

8.2 **Title and Risk.** Title and risk of loss pass to Buyer upon delivery to the carrier.

8.3 **Racks.** Glass racks remain Supplier's property. Buyer shall return empty racks to Supplier within sixty days after delivery or pay Supplier's then-current replacement charge.

8.4 **Labeling.** Each insulating glass unit shall bear a permanent label identifying Supplier, the date of manufacture and the applicable IGCC certification.

## 9. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE

9.1 **Inspection.** Buyer shall inspect Products within ten Business Days after arrival at the delivery location and notify Supplier in writing of any visible damage, breakage or nonconformity.

9.2 **Nonconforming Products.** Supplier shall, at its option and cost, replace or credit any nonconforming Product notified under Section 9.1 or Section 10.3, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver replacements within the lead times set out in Exhibit A.

## 10. WARRANTY

10.1 **Product Warranty.** Supplier warrants that each Product will (a) conform to the Specifications at delivery; (b) be free from defects in material and workmanship; and (c) for a period of ten years from the date of manufacture, be free from material obstruction of vision caused by film formation or dust collection on the interior glass surfaces resulting from failure of the hermetic seal, under normal use and installation in accordance with Supplier's published glazing guidelines.

10.2 **Coating Warranty.** Supplier warrants that the low-E coating on each Product will not peel, crack or deteriorate for a period of ten years from the date of manufacture.

10.3 **Remedy.** Buyer shall notify Supplier of any warranty claim within sixty days after discovery. Supplier's obligation under this Section 10 is to furnish a replacement Product, delivered to the Project site, and to reimburse Buyer's reasonable documented labor costs to remove the defective unit and install the replacement, up to an aggregate amount per unit equal to two times the Price of that unit.

10.4 **Disclaimer.** EXCEPT AS STATED IN THIS SECTION 10, SUPPLIER MAKES NO OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

## 11. INDEMNIFICATION

11.1 **By Supplier.** Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Buyer and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, members, managers and employees, from and against all third-party claims, losses, damages, liabilities and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from (a) bodily injury, death or property damage caused by a defect in a Product; (b) any claim that a Product infringes a third party's patent, trademark or other intellectual property right; or (c) Supplier's negligence or willful misconduct.

11.2 **By Buyer.** Buyer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Supplier and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors and employees, from and against all third-party claims, losses, damages, liabilities and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from (a) Buyer's design, fabrication or installation of facade systems, except to the extent caused by a defect in

 a Product; or (b) Buyer's negligence or willful misconduct.

11.3 **Procedure.** The indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of a claim, allow the indemnifying Party to control the defense and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing an obligation on the indemnified Party may be made without its consent), and reasonably cooperate at the indemnifying Party's expense.

## 12. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

12.1 **Exclusion.** Neither Party is liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages, or for lost profits, arising out of this Agreement, except for liability under Section 11 or Section 14, or for a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

12.2 **Cap.** Except for liability under Section 11 or Section 14, for a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or for Buyer's payment obligations for Products, each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement in any contract year shall not exceed the total Prices paid and payable by Buyer for Products in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

## 13. INSURANCE

13.1 **Supplier Coverage.** During the Term and for three years afterward, Supplier shall maintain, with insurers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best: (a) commercial general liability insurance, including products-completed operations coverage, of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) umbrella or excess liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence and in the aggregate; (c) automobile liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 combined single limit; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by law, with employer's liability of at least $1,000,000.

13.2 **Additional Insured; Certificates.** Supplier shall cause Buyer to be named as an additional insured on the policies described in Sections 13.1(a) and 13.1(b), and shall deliver certificates of insurance to Buyer upon execution of this Agreement, upon each policy renewal and upon Buyer's reasonable request. Supplier shall give Buyer at least thirty days' prior written notice of any cancellation or material reduction of coverage.

## 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

14.1 **Obligation.** Each Party shall keep confidential, and use only for purposes of this Agreement, all non-public information disclosed by the other Party, including pricing, Specifications, Project information and forecasts, and shall not disclose it except to its and its Affiliates' employees, advisors, lenders and insurers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality at least as protective.

14.2 **Exceptions.** Section 14.1 does not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving Party, was lawfully known to the receiving Party before disclosure, is independently developed, or is required to be disclosed by law or court order (after prompt notice to the disclosing Party where lawful).

14.3 **Duration.** The obligations in this Section 14 continue for three years after the end of the Term.

## 15. TERMINATION

15.1 **For Breach.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty days after receiving written notice describing it (or ten days for a failure to pay undisputed amounts).

15.2 **Insolvency.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, has a receiver appointed for its business or assets, or becomes the subject of any voluntary or involuntary bankruptcy proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty days.

15.3 **Effect.** Upon termination, Buyer shall pay for all Products delivered and all Products in production under accepted Purchase Orders. Sections 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15.3, 16.2 and 17 survive expiration or termination.

## 16. ASSIGNMENT

16.1 **General.** Neither Party may assign or delegate this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations under it, whether voluntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section 16 is void. This Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

16.2 **Change of Control of Buyer.** Any Change of Control of Buyer shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Buyer and requires Supplier's prior written consent. If a Change of Control of Buyer occurs without Supplier's prior written consent, Supplier may terminate this Agreement by written notice to Buyer, and Buyer shall pay Supplier, within thirty days after that notice, the Price for all remaining Committed Quantities under all open Statements of Work, whether or not those Products have been ordered, manufactured or delivered.

## 17. GENERAL

17.1 **Governing Law; Venue.** This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules, and by Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code as adopted in Pennsylvania. Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania for any action arising out of this Agreement.

17.2 **Notices.** All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses below (or to another address a Party designates by notice), with a copy by email. A notice is effective upon receipt.

> If to Supplier: Meideis Glassworks, Inc., 2200 Furnace Road, Allentown, Pennsylvania 18109, Attention: Vice President, Commercial Sales; email: contracts@meideisglass.com
>
> If to Buyer: Besouth Facade Systems, LLC, 410 Wharf Street, Camden, New Jersey 08103, Attention: President; email: legal@besouthfacade.com

17.3 **Amendme

nts; Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving Party, and no failure or delay in exercising any right operates as a waiver of it.

17.4 **Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict among the documents comprising the Parties' agreement, the following order of precedence applies: first, Amendment No. 1 (and any subsequent written amendment to this Agreement executed by both Parties); second, this Agreement, including its Exhibits; and third, any Statement of Work.

17.5 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party is liable for failure or delay in performance (other than payment obligations) caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, acts of God, war, terrorism, labor disputes not involving the affected Party's own employees, government action or failure of utilities, provided the affected Party promptly notifies the other Party and uses commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance. If a force majeure event prevents Supplier from delivering Products for more than thirty days, Section 5.2 applies to the affected quantities.

17.6 **Independent Contractors.** The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture or agency relationship.

17.7 **Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force, and the invalid provision shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted.

17.8 **Counterparts; Electronic Signatures.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument. Signatures delivered by PDF or electronic signature service are binding.

## EXHIBIT A
### PRODUCTS AND SPECIFICATIONS

1. **Product Description.** Factory-sealed, dual-pane low-E coated insulating glass units for commercial curtain-wall, window-wall and storefront applications, consisting of:
   - (a) outboard lite: 6 mm heat-strengthened or fully tempered clear or low-iron float glass, with sputtered (soft-coat) low-E coating on the No. 2 surface, from Supplier's standard coating series MG-50, MG-62 and MG-70;
   - (b) airspace: 12.7 mm (1/2 inch), 90% argon fill, with warm-edge stainless steel or structural silicone-compatible spacer;
   - (c) inboard lite: 6 mm heat-strengthened, fully tempered or annealed clear float glass;
   - (d) dual seal: polyisobutylene primary seal and structural silicone secondary seal.
2. **Standards.** Products shall be certified by the Insulating Glass Certification Council (IGCC) to ASTM E2190, and glass substrates shall conform to ASTM C1036 and, where heat-treated, ASTM C1048.
3. **Size Limits.** Maximum unit size 84 inches by 144 inches; minimum unit size 10 inches by 24 inches.
4. **Lead Times.** Standard lead time is six weeks from Purchase Order acceptance; replacement units for nonconforming Products, three weeks.

## EXHIBIT B
### PRICING

| Product Configuration | Price per sq. ft. (FCA Allentown) |
|---|---|
| MG-50 low-E IGU, clear/clear, HS outboard | $24.50 |
| MG-62 low-E IGU, clear/clear, HS outboard | $27.75 |
| MG-70 low-E IGU, low-iron/clear, HS outboard | $33.10 |
| Fully tempered upcharge (per lite) | $2.40 |
| Units exceeding 50 sq. ft. (oversize upcharge) | 15% |

Prices are subject to adjustment under Section 6.2 and do not apply to Committed Quantities under a Statement of Work with separately stated pricing under Section 6.3.

# STATEMENT OF WORK NO. 2026-03

## Calloway Street Tower Facade

This Statement of Work No. 2026-03 (this "**Statement of Work**") is entered into as of March 2, 2026 (the "**SOW Date**") by and between **Meideis Glassworks, Inc.**, a Pennsylvania corporation ("**Supplier**"), and **Besouth Facade Systems, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"). It is entered into under the Supply Agreement between Supplier and Buyer dated as of April 1, 2023 (the "**Agreement**").

Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Statement of Work have the meanings given in the Agreement. Under Section 2.2 of the Agreement, this Statement of Work is incorporated into and governed by the Agreement.

## 1. PROJECT

1.1 **Project.** The Project is the Calloway Street Tower facade, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (the "**Calloway Project**").

1.2 **Project Description.** The Calloway Project is a 31-story mixed-use office and residential tower at 1650 Calloway Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19103. Buyer is the curtain-wall subcontractor and will design, fabricate and install a unitized curtain-wall system on all four elevations from Level 3 through the roof parapet.

1.3 **Project Parties.**

| Role | Entity |
|---|---|
| Owner | Calloway Street Partners, LP |
| General Contractor | Delmont Keane Builders, Inc. |
| Architect of Record | Varga Holloway Architects |
| Curtain-Wall Subcontractor | Besouth Facade Systems, LLC |
| Glass Supplier | Meideis Glassworks, Inc. |

1.4 **Buyer's Project Reference.** Buyer Job No. B-2611. Buyer shall cite this number on every Purchase Order issued under this Statement of Work.

## 2. PRODUCTS AND PROJECT SPECIFICATIONS

2.1 **Products.** Supplier shall supply Products of the following configurations for the Calloway Project, each conforming to Exhibit A of the Agreement:

| Type | Configuration | Location |
|---|---|---|
| IG-1 | MG-62 low-E IGU, clear/clear, 6 mm HS outboard / 12.7 mm argon-filled airspace / 6 mm HS inboard | Typical vision glass, Levels 3–31 |
| IG-2 | MG-70 low-E IGU, low-iron/clear, 6 mm HS outboard / 12.7 mm argon-filled airspace / 6 mm FT inboard | Podium and lobby vision glass, Levels 3–5 |

2.2 **Project-Specific Specifications.** In addition to Exhibit A of the Agreement, Products supplied under this Statement of Work shall comply with the following, which Supplier accepts as Specifications for the Calloway Project:

- (a) Architect's Specification Section 08 44 13 (Glazed Aluminum Curtain Walls) and Section 08 81 00 (Glass Glazing), Issued for Construction set dated January 9, 2026, to the extent applicable to insulating glass units;
- (b) center-of-glass U-factor of 0.29 Btu/hr·ft²·°F or lower for IG-1 and 0.28 or lower for IG-2, calculated per NFRC 100;
- (c) heat-strengthened lites to have a roller-wave distortion not exceeding 0.003 inch peak-to-valley, with rollerwave oriented horizontally;
- (d) warm-edge spacers in black finish; and
- (e) structural silicone secondary seal compatible with Buyer's structural glazing sealant, as confirmed by Supplier's adhesion and compatibility test report to be furnished before the first production run.

2.3 **Mock-Up.** Supplier shall supply, at the Prices in Section 4, units for Buyer's visual mock-up and performance mock-up, within four weeks after Buyer's Purchase Order for them. Mock-up quantities count toward the Committed Quantity.

## 3. COMMITTED QUANTITY

3.1 **Committed Quantity.** The Committed Quantity under this Statement of Work is 42,000 square feet of insulating glass units, allocated by type as follows:

| Type | Committed Quantity (sq. ft. of finished unit area) |
|---|---|
| IG-1 | 36,500 |
| IG-2 | 5,500 |
| **Total** | **42,000** |

3.2 **Measurement.** Quantities are measured as finished unit area, in accordance with Section 6.1 of the Agreement, with each unit rounded up to the nearest whole square foot.

3.3 **Changes.** The Committed Quantity may be increased or reduced only as provided in Section 2.3 of the Agreement. Buyer may reallocate quantities between IG-1 and IG-2 by written notice to Supplier before release of the affected Purchase Order to production, without changing the total Committed Quantity.

## 4. PRICING

4.1 **Project Prices.** The following Prices apply to the Committed Quantity under this Statement of Work and, under Section 6.3 of the Agreement, are fixed and not subject to adjustment under Section 6.2 of the Agreement:

| Type | Price per sq. ft. (FCA Allentown) |
|---|---|
| IG-1 | $28.40 |
| IG-2 | $35.15 |

4.2 **Upcharges.** The fully tempered upcharge and oversize upcharge in Exhibit B of the Agreement apply at the rates stated there. The Project Prices above already include the fully tempered inboard lite for IG-2.

4.3 **Freight.** At Buyer's request under Section 8.1 of the Agreement, Supplier shall arrange freight to Buyer's fabrication facility at 410 Wharf Street, Camden, New Jersey 08103, at Buyer's cost, billed at carrier's rates without markup.

## 5. DELIVERY SCHEDULE

5.1 **Release Schedule.** Buyer shall issue Purchase Orders in releases tied to its unit fabrication sequence. The target schedule is:

| Release | Scope | Target Delivery to Buyer's Facility |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mock-up units | May 2026 |
| 2 | Levels 3–8 (IG-1 and all IG-2) | August 2026 |
| 3 | Levels 9–16 | November 2026 |
| 4 | Levels 17–24 | February 2027 |
| 5 | Levels 25–31 and parapet | May 2027 |

5.2 **Lead Times.** Purchase Orders under this Statement of Work are subject to the standard lead times in Exhibit A of the Agreement. Buyer shall issue each release Purchase Order at least the standard lead time before the requested delivery date.

5.3 **Schedule Adjustments.** Buyer may defer any release by up to sixty days by written notice given at least three weeks before the confirmed delivery date. Deferral does not reduce the Committed Quantity.

5.4 **Attic Stock.** Buyer's Purchase Orders will include attic stock as required by the Project spec

calloway_tower_statement_of_work.md, page 2 of 2:
ifications. Attic stock units count toward the Committed Quantity.

## 6. PROJECT SUBMITTALS AND QUALITY

6.1 **Submittals.** Within fifteen Business Days after the SOW Date, Supplier shall furnish to Buyer, for submission to the Architect: product data sheets; NFRC performance calculations for IG-1 and IG-2; IGCC certification; glass samples (12 inches by 12 inches) of each type; and Supplier's standard warranty forms reflecting Section 10 of the Agreement.

6.2 **Quality Control.** Supplier shall retain production inspection records for each release for the warranty periods in Section 10 of the Agreement and make them available to Buyer on reasonable request.

6.3 **Project Labeling.** In addition to the labeling required by Section 8.4 of the Agreement, each unit shall bear a removable label stating Buyer's Job No. B-2611, the unit mark number and the type designation.

## 7. PROJECT CONTACTS

| | Supplier | Buyer |
|---|---|---|
| Commercial | Dana R. Whitcombe, Regional Sales Manager | Marcus T. Ilves, Project Manager |
| Technical | Priya Venkataraman, Technical Services Manager | Joelle A. Brandt, Engineering Manager |

Project communications may be directed to these contacts. Notices under the Agreement must be given in accordance with Section 17.2 of the Agreement.

## 8. GENERAL

8.1 **Governing Terms.** Except as expressly set out in this Statement of Work, all terms of the Agreement apply to the Calloway Project.

8.2 **Status.** This Statement of Work is open, within the meaning of Section 2.2 of the Agreement, until Supplier has delivered, and Buyer has paid for, the full Committed Quantity.

8.3 **Counterparts.** This Statement of Work may be executed in counterparts and by PDF or electronic signature in accordance with Section 17.8 of the Agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Statement of Work as of the SOW Date.

# AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Amendment No. 1 to Supply Agreement (this "**Amendment**") is entered into as of October 20, 2026 (the "**Amendment Date**") by and between **Meideis Glassworks, Inc.**, a Pennsylvania corporation with its principal place of business at 2200 Furnace Road, Allentown, Pennsylvania 18109 ("**Supplier**"), and **Besouth Facade Systems, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal place of business at 410 Wharf Street, Camden, New Jersey 08103 ("**Buyer**"). Supplier and Buyer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier and Buyer are parties to a Supply Agreement dated as of April 1, 2023 (the "**Agreement**").

B. Supplier and Buyer are parties to Statement of Work No. 2026-03 under the Agreement, dated as of March 2, 2026, for the Calloway Street Tower facade, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (the "**Calloway SOW**").

C. The Architect of Record for the Calloway Project has issued a revision to the Project's glass glazing specification calling for laminated heat-strengthened spandrel glass at the floor-line and column-cover zones of the unitized curtain wall. Buyer wishes to purchase, and Supplier wishes to supply, that spandrel glass under the Agreement and the Calloway SOW.

D. Under Section 17.3 of the Agreement, the Agreement may be amended by a written instrument signed by both Parties.

The Parties therefore agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 **Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Amendment have the meanings given in the Agreement.

1.2 **References.** On and after the Amendment Date, each reference in the Agreement to "this Agreement," and each reference in any Statement of Work to "the Agreement," means the Agreement as amended by this Amendment.

## 2. AMENDMENTS TO THE AGREEMENT

2.1 **Products.** Section 1.7 of the Agreement is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following, which applies for all purposes of the Agreement:

> 1.7 "**Products**" means all architectural glass products manufactured, fabricated or supplied by Supplier, including the low-E coated insulating glass units described in Exhibit A and the laminated spandrel glass described in Exhibit A-1.

2.2 **Specifications.** Section 1.10 of the Agreement is amended by replacing the words "set out in Exhibit A" with "set out in Exhibit A and Exhibit A-1."

2.3 **New Exhibit A-1.** The Agreement is amended by adding Exhibit A-1 (Laminated Spandrel Glass), in the form attached to this Amendment, immediately following Exhibit A.

2.4 **Pricing.** Exhibit B of the Agreement is amended by adding the following rows to the pricing table, immediately following the row for "Units exceeding 50 sq. ft. (oversize upcharge)":
